moves.headline: Dell falls 12% before its results as AI server stocks give back Monday’s rally
moves.summary: Dell fell 11.8% to $295.28 during the session ahead of its third-quarter report, after jumping 20% the day before. AI hardware stocks retreated, and HPE’s 16% drop after its own report raised worries about component shortages and margins in AI servers.
why: Dell had rallied 20.5% on November 23 when Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. The next day the AI trade reversed, Nvidia fell about 6–7%, and HPE dropped 16% after warning that AI server component shortages could last into 2028. Benzinga reported that the shortage concerns spread to Dell, and investors cut positions before Dell’s results.

After the close Dell reported record revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103%, a record $132.3 billion AI backlog and full-year guidance raised to $202 billion, with a $25 billion increase to its buyback authorisation. The shares were roughly flat in after-hours trading.
context: On November 24 the Nasdaq fell about 1.5% and the S&P 500 about 0.5% while the Dow rose almost 0.9%, as chip stocks gave back much of the previous day’s rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. Nvidia fell about 6–7% and AMD, Micron and Broadcom also dropped.
Money rotated out of semiconductors and AI hardware into health care, consumer staples and retailers, so most stocks rose even as the technology-heavy indexes fell.
